subject.title: [Feature]: Auto-discovery of agent configurations from external workspaces

question: Should OpenClaw add core trusted external-workspace agent-config discovery, or keep registration explicit and improve the existing agent management path instead?
rationale: The requested feature adds a new public config surface, filesystem scanning, trust boundaries, and live routing semantics that cannot be safely chosen by cleanup automation.

options.title: Keep explicit registration
options.body: Continue using `agents.list`, `$include`, `openclaw agents add`, and `agents.create/update/delete`, and document or improve batch/operator tooling without adding core glob discovery.

options.title: Design trusted discovery
options.body: Define a core discovery contract with trusted roots, allowed file names, validation, precedence, reload behavior, agentDir/session isolation, and security proof before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to zero-restart management first
options.body: Improve explicit runtime registration and binding reload semantics before deciding whether external workspace glob discovery belongs in core.

recommendation.title: Keep explicit registration
recommendation.body: Continue using `agents.list`, `$include`, `openclaw agents add`, and `agents.create/update/delete`, and document or improve batch/operator tooling without adding core glob discovery.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is on the model-visible `agents_list` discovery surface and adjacent multi-agent workflow docs/tests.
